title: Old-object word generation after freely contracting a formal cone
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\mathcal A$ a small $R$-linear cochain dg category, and $u:x\to y$ a closed degree-zero arrow. Use the free adjoining constructions of [lem-coef-dgcat-free-cell-calculus] and the labelled cone enlargement of [lem-coef-dgcat-formal-cone-enlargement]. Let $\mathcal L$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Cone}(\mathcal A)$ on the labelled representables and $Z=C_u$. Let $\mathcal T=\mathcal L\langle h:Z\to Z,\ |h|=-1,\ dh=1_Z\rangle$, and let $\mathcal T_0$ be its full subcategory on the representable labels. Identify those labels with the objects of $\mathcal A$. Write $\iota_y,\pi_y,\iota_x,\pi_x$ for the graded cone inclusions and projections of degrees $0,0,-1,1$, respectively, and put
$$v_h=\pi_xh\iota_y,\quad a_h=\pi_xh\iota_x,\quad b_h=-\pi_yh\iota_y,\quad w_h=-\pi_yh\iota_x.$$

The underlying graded $R$-linear category of $\mathcal T_0$ is generated by the images of all homogeneous arrows of $\mathcal A$ together with $v_h,a_h,b_h,w_h$. Explicitly, every homogeneous arrow between representable labels is a finite $R$-linear combination of composable words in these arrows and coefficients from $\mathcal A$. The expansion uses the graded identities
$$1_Z=\iota_y\pi_y+\iota_x\pi_x,\qquad h=-\iota_y b_h\pi_y-\iota_y w_h\pi_x+\iota_x v_h\pi_y+\iota_x a_h\pi_x.$$
In particular, two graded $R$-linear functors from $\mathcal T_0$ to any graded $R$-linear category, with the same object map and agreeing on the image of $\mathcal A$ and on $v_h,a_h,b_h,w_h$, are equal. Here a graded $R$-linear category has graded $R$-modules of arrows and degree-additive unital associative composition, and a graded $R$-linear functor preserves that data. No assertion that the coordinate inclusions and projections are closed is made.

source.place: Chapter 1, section 1.3.1, Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29; comparison construction and inverse verification, using Proposition 1.7, printed p. 27. General closed-arrow formulation and explicit cochain signs by the agent. Read online; no local archive or corresponding Stacks tag.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-dgcat-free-cell-calculus] to $\mathcal L$, with $s=t=Z$, $e=h$, $n=-1$ and attaching cycle $1_Z$. The identity is closed, so this is an allowed free adjunction. The exhaustive word filtration and its graded-split quotients imply that every homogeneous arrow $X\to Y$ in $\mathcal T$, for representable labels $X,Y$, is a finite sum of homogeneous words $a_mh a_{m-1}h\cdots h a_0$. Here $a_0:X\to Z$, $a_m:Z\to Y$, and the intermediate $a_j:Z\to Z$ lie in $\mathcal L$; the length-zero words lie in $\mathcal L(X,Y)$. Indeed pure homogeneous tensors generate each quotient; lift each tensor to the corresponding word, subtract it, and induct on the finite filtration length. Thus no completed or infinite words are needed.

source.place: Chapter 1, §1.3.1, proof of Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29: representable/cone enlargement and inverse verification. Explicit graded-word calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Use the graded coordinate maps and identities of [lem-coef-dgcat-formal-cone-enlargement], restricted to the full subcategory $\mathcal L$. Put $z_y=y$ and $z_x=x$, and $c_{\alpha\beta}=\pi_\alpha h\iota_\beta:z_\beta\to z_\alpha$ for $\alpha,\beta\in\{y,x\}$. Their degrees, in the order $(yy,yx,xy,xx)$, are $(-1,-2,0,-1)$. By the definitions in the item, these four entries are $(-b_h,-w_h,v_h,a_h)$. The coordinate identity $1_Z=\iota_y\pi_y+\iota_x\pi_x$ holds in $\mathcal T$, since its inclusion from $\mathcal L$ preserves sums and compositions.

source.place: Chapter 1, §1.3.1, proof of Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29: representable/cone enlargement and inverse verification. Explicit graded-word calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Multiply the identity of step 2 on both sides of $h$: $h=(\iota_y\pi_y+\iota_x\pi_x)h(\iota_y\pi_y+\iota_x\pi_x)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta}\iota_\alpha c_{\alpha\beta}\pi_\beta$. Substituting the four entries from step 2 is exactly $h=-\iota_y b_h\pi_y-\iota_y w_h\pi_x+\iota_x v_h\pi_y+\iota_x a_h\pi_x$. Every summand has degree $-1$. This uses bilinearity and associativity only; no factors are interchanged, so there are no extra Koszul signs.

source.place: Chapter 1, §1.3.1, proof of Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29: representable/cone enlargement and inverse verification. Explicit graded-word calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: In a positive-length word from step 1 replace each of its $m$ occurrences of $h$ by the four-term expression of step 3 and distribute. Each of the at most $4^m$ resulting summands is a composable word in the entries $c_{\alpha\beta}$ with coefficients of the forms $a_m\iota_\alpha$, $\pi_\beta a_j\iota_\gamma$, and $\pi_\delta a_0$. These coefficients are homogeneous morphisms in $\mathcal L$ between representable labels. The embedding clause of [lem-coef-dgcat-formal-cone-enlargement] identifies each with an actual homogeneous arrow of $\mathcal A$, preserving units and composition. The same clause identifies every length-zero term with an arrow of $\mathcal A$. Replacing $c_{yy},c_{yx},c_{xy},c_{xx}$ by $-b_h,-w_h,v_h,a_h$ now gives the required finite linear combination in $\mathcal T_0$. All intermediate labels after expansion are old labels; no coordinate map with endpoint $Z$ remains. The total degree is preserved by each substitution.

source.place: Chapter 1, §1.3.1, proof of Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29: representable/cone enlargement and inverse verification. Explicit graded-word calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Let $F,G$ be the two graded $R$-linear functors in the conclusion. Their common object map identifies the targets of their arrow maps. They agree on each coefficient from $\mathcal A$ and each of the four extra generators. Induction on the number of factors, using preservation of composition and identities, gives agreement on each composable word; preservation of finite sums and scalar multiplication gives agreement on every finite linear combination. Step 4 covers all homogeneous arrows. For an arbitrary element of a graded Hom module, its homogeneous components are finite, so additivity gives agreement there too. Hence the functors are equal. No calculation used closedness of a coordinate inclusion or projection, or imposed $h^2=0$.
